answer: An operator may name its agents onyx, velvet and ivory, yet all should share one voting allowance. An independent registry verifies the ultimate owner and issues a credential; each agent proves it in zero knowledge, revealing the same epoch-specific nullifier. The ledger pools votes under that nullifier, so aliases and shell companies cannot multiply the owner's quota. No public identity list is needed. This relies on reliable ownership checks: nominees or a corrupt issuer can still create extra credentials, so issuer audits matter.
